subject: Standard normal deviates and model predictions

messages.author: feaba58d41c5a493
messages.subject: Standard normal deviates and model predictions
parts:
Dear unmarked users-

I am fitting N-mixture models to bird data with linear and quadratic predictor variables for vegetation structure, which are continuous and have been transformed to standard normal deviates (SND's) per sampling point ((obs value - mean value)/SD of obs values).  So I fit a model to these data and calculate model predictions, but the preds are unreasonable when calculated within the range (min:max obs values) of a veg variable on the normal (non-transformed) scale.  I get reasonable predictions when calculated in the mix:max range of the SND's, but then the x-axis values are on the transformed scale (e.g., -1.7 to 4 for grass density) rather than the real scale of values (0.0-8.0).  Does any one have any recommendations to make this prediction process more efficient?

For example, could someone recommend code for 1) transforming observed data to SND's in an R object (rather than doing so manually in the csv file), and 2) back-transforming from SND's prior to making predictions so that the values of the predictor variable are on the original scale?  Here are some example Bobolink and grass density data and code.  Thanks so much for your input.

Matt
______________________________________
Matt Giovanni
Postdoctoral Visiting Research Fellow
Canadian Wildlife Service
Prairie and Northern Region
Environment Canada
2365 Albert St., Room 300
Regina, SK S4P 4K1
306-780-5308 work
402-617-3764 mobile
Research website:
http://sites.google.com/site/matthewgiovanni/


<<BOBO model.R>>

<<BOBO data.csv>>
library(unmarked)
umf=csvToUMF("BOBO veg.csv",long=FALSE,type="unmarkedFramePCount")

### model fit to observed values of grass density
grass2=pcount(~1 ~GRASS+GRASS2+offset(log(AREA)),umf)
summary(grass2)
DF=data.frame(GRASS=seq(0,6,0.5),GRASS2=(seq(0,6,0.5))^2,AREA=10)
predict(grass2,type="state",newdata=DF,backTran=TRUE,appendData=FALSE)

### model fit to standard normal deviates of grass density values
grass2=pcount(~1 ~sGRASS+sGRASS2+offset(log(AREA)),umf)
summary(grass2)
# preds on SND scale for grass density are okay
DF=data.frame(sGRASS=seq(-1.7,2.5,0.5),sGRASS2=(seq(-1.7,2.5,0.5))^2,AREA=10)
predict(grass2,type="state",newdata=DF,backTran=TRUE,appendData=FALSE)
# preds on original scale of grass density are inflated
DF=data.frame(sGRASS=seq(0,6,0.5),sGRASS2=(seq(0,6,0.5))^2,AREA=10)
predict(grass2,type="state",newdata=DF,backTran=TRUE,appendData=FALSE)

hi Matt,
 the predictions should be made on the transformed scale. You can plot by back-transforming the covariate axis. i.e., plot(predicted, x*sigmax + mux)
where sigmax and mux are the observed SD and mean of the covariate.
regards,
andy

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Standard normal deviates and model predictions
parts:
Hi Matt,

Standardizing the covariates in unmarked is very easy. See

vignette('unmarked')

After you have your unmarkedFrame, you can do something like:

obsCovs(umf) <- scale(obsCovs(umf))

You just need to keep track of the original mean and SD for each covariate so that you can back-transform the way Andy indicated.

Richard

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Standard normal deviates and model predictions
parts:
Hi Matt,

I would pull out the siteCovs, manipulate them, and then add them back to the unmarkedFrame. Something like this should work:

sc <- siteCovs(umf)
sc[,11:27] <- scale(sc[,11:27])
siteCovs(sc) <- sc


Richard

Hi Matt,

Standardizing the covariates in unmarked is very easy. See

vignette('unmarked')

After you have your unmarkedFrame, you can do something like:

obsCovs(umf) <- scale(obsCovs(umf))

You just need to keep track of the original mean and SD for each covariate so that you can back-transform the way Andy indicated.

Richard
